name: padding_access(type, ctx, prev_field, sz)
prose: Generated functions padding_ctx_access_<ctx> (from the macro padding_access(type, ctx, prev_field, sz), verifier_ctx.c:265-278, instantiated at lines 281, 284, 287, 290 and 293 for bpf_sock_addr, bpf_sk_lookup, __sk_buff, bpf_sock and sk_reuseport_md); each is a __naked BPF program in the given section taking no arguments. Precondition: none. Postcondition of each generated program: its assembly body loads sz bytes from the context pointer in r1 at offsetofend(struct ctx, prev_field), sets r0 = 0 and exits (returning 0 if it were run). The instantiations are annotated with the verifier's expected outcome: the sk_lookup one (bpf_sk_lookup, after remote_port, 2 bytes) is annotated __success, the other four (cgroup/bind4 after msg_src_ip6[3], tc after tstamp_type, cgroup/post_bind4 after dst_port, sk_reuseport after hash) are annotated __failure with the message 'invalid bpf_context access'.
note: unreviewed (round15 fixed-unreviewed); re-read verifier_ctx.c:265-293; prose of the old version essentially unchanged; name set to the macro definition head (method rule 5) since the packet name padding_ctx_access is a template for five generated functions.

name: from_positive_unknown_to_4
prose: A __naked BPF program (section tracepoint) taking no arguments, annotated __success (the verifier must accept the bounded loop). Precondition: none. Postcondition (verifier_loops1.c:37-48): it calls bpf_get_prandom_u32, which leaves a 32-bit value zero-extended in the 64-bit register r0, so r0 is in [0, 2^32 - 1]. The test 'if r0 s< 0 goto exit' is a 64-bit signed comparison and is therefore never taken for that range. It then loops 'r0 += 1; if r0 < 4 goto loop' with 64-bit unsigned arithmetic, so r0 is incremented at least once and until it is at least 4, and it exits returning that r0, a value between 4 and 2^32 (2^32 when the random value was 2^32 - 1).
note: reviewer (round15) right: the branch is a 64-bit signed compare on a zero-extended u32 helper result so the negative path never runs (verifier_loops1.c:41); the old prose's 'sign bit set' path was wrong, and its claim that the final r0 is >= 4 is true for every path.

name: from_totally_unknown_to_4
prose: A __naked BPF program (section tracepoint) taking no arguments, annotated __success. Precondition: none. Postcondition (verifier_loops1.c:53-63): it calls bpf_get_prandom_u32, leaving a 32-bit value zero-extended in the 64-bit register r0, then loops 'r0 += 1; if r0 < 4 goto loop' using 64-bit arithmetic and an unsigned 64-bit comparison, so the increment does not wrap at 2^32; r0 is incremented at least once and until it is at least 4. It exits returning that r0, which is between 4 and 2^32 (2^32 when the random value was 2^32 - 1).
note: reviewer (round15) right: the increment is 64-bit with no modulo-2^32 wrap (final r0 can be 2^32); the round-0 reviewer's 'negative initial values exit with r0 < 4' does not apply because the helper result is zero-extended and no sign test exists in this program.

name: map_equal
prose: Precondition: lru_map and expected are open BPF map file descriptors whose values have nr_cpus per-CPU slots (the global nr_cpus is positive). Postcondition (map_equal, test_lru_map.c:116-119 with map_subset at 93-114): it returns map_subset(lru_map, expected) && map_subset(expected, lru_map), so the second call is made only if the first returned nonzero. map_subset(map0, map1) iterates over the keys of map1 (starting from next_key = 0 as the 'previous' key) and, for each one, asserts that the lookup in map1 succeeds (an assertion failure aborts the program), looks the key up in map0 and returns 0 (after printing a message) if it is not found there or if the first per-CPU value (value[0]) differs; it returns 1 when the iteration ends. So map_equal returns 1 exactly when every key of expected is found in lru_map and every key of lru_map is found in expected, each with the same value in slot 0 (other CPU slots are not compared), and 0 otherwise. No descriptors are closed.
note: reviewer (round15) right: a failed lookup in map0 returns 0 rather than asserting (test_lru_map.c:101-106); only the lookup in the iterated map (line 100) asserts; round-1 reviewer's value[0]-only point was already in the old prose; round-2's claim that iteration failure aborts is not what the old prose said.

name: __send_pkts
prose: Precondition: ifobject and xsk are valid, xsk->pkt_stream and ifobject->umem are non-NULL, xsk->xsk is a valid AF_XDP socket, xsk->batch_size is positive, buffer_len computed from umem and pkt_stream->max_pkt_len is positive, and pkts_in_flight is the global in-flight counter (read without the lock at the pacing check, updated under pacing_mutex later). Postcondition: if pkts_in_flight is at least (int)((umem_size(umem) - xsk->batch_size * buffer_len) / buffer_len), the function calls kick_tx and returns TEST_FAILURE if kick_tx fails, otherwise TEST_CONTINUE, without submitting descriptors or changing pkts_in_flight; otherwise it reserves TX descriptors, may call complete_pkts(xsk, xsk->batch_size) in the reserve loop while ignoring that call's return value, fills and submits i descriptors to the TX ring, cancels the packet stream and the remaining reserved descriptors if a packet needs more fragments than remain in the batch, generates umem data only for packets whose pkt->valid is true, increments xsk->outstanding_tx by the number of valid fragments, and increments pkts_in_flight by the number of valid packets under pacing_mutex; it returns TEST_FAILURE if a reserve-loop poll fails when use_poll is true (negative when timeout is true, or non-positive when timeout is false), if a post-submit poll fails when use_poll is true (non-positive unless ret == 0 and timeout is true), or if complete_pkts(xsk, i) fails on the non-timeout path; it returns TEST_PASS if a poll returns 0 while timeout is true (in either poll) or after complete_pkts succeeds on the non-timeout path; and it returns TEST_CONTINUE after a successful kick_tx at the pacing limit, or when timeout is true and either use_poll is false or the post-submit poll returns positive, after submitting whatever descriptors were reserved (possibly fewer than a full batch); pacing_mutex is locked and unlocked only around the pkts_in_flight update and is not held on return.
note: reviewer (round15) right: the pacing check reads pkts_in_flight without pacing_mutex (test_xsk.c:1115) and only the later update at 1199-1201 takes the lock; precondition corrected. Rest of the prose re-read against test_xsk.c:1104-1226 and kept (round-1/2 points already reflected).

name: dut_run
prose: Precondition: skel is a loaded xdp_features skeleton; env.ifname/env.ifindex name the device under test; a controller is expected to connect to DUT_CTRL_PORT. Postcondition (dut_run, xdp_features.c:360-493): it starts a reuseport server on the control port; if that returns NULL it prints a message and returns -errno. It accepts one connection; on failure it frees the listening fds and returns -errno. It then loops while the global exiting is false, receiving TLV commands (a failed recv_msg just continues the loop): CMD_START (ignored if state already is CMD_START; state is not initialized before its first use) attaches the XDP program and, if that fails, jumps to out with the error, then starts the echo thread and jumps to out if it fails (these two paths skip pthread_join), then sends an ACK and jumps to end_thread if send fails; CMD_STOP (only if started) sets exiting, detaches the program, sends an ACK and goes to end_thread with send's result in err; CMD_GET_XDP_CAP and CMD_GET_STATS query the XDP features or the stats map, jump to end_thread with the error if the query fails, and otherwise send an ACK carrying the data (a send failure goes to end_thread); other commands are ignored. end_thread joins the echo thread (dut_thread, which is 0 if no thread was created); out then detaches the XDP program from env.ifindex, closes the control socket and frees the listening fds. The function returns err, which is the last value it was assigned: a negative error, 0, or the positive byte count of the last successful send (for example after CMD_STOP).
note: reviewer (round15) right: the echo thread is not joined when XDP attach or echo-thread creation fails (goto out at xdp_features.c:402-407 skips pthread_join at 486); round-0 reviewer's 'positive send() byte count' point was already in the old prose.

name: main
prose: Precondition: argc/argv are the command line (read_args fills ifname, ifindex and the launch-time options); the interface exists, and the process can run the 'sudo tc' and 'sudo ethtool' commands it issues. Postcondition (main, xdp_hw_metadata.c:735-894; slice cut the head): it reads the rx queue count, calls error(1, ...) (which prints and terminates the process with status 1) if launch_time_queue is out of range, cleans existing configurations, sleeps 1 s and enables hardware timestamping. It builds the tc priority map and the queue map strings with asprintf/realloc; a failure of any of these allocations prints a message and goes to free_mem (freeing buf, map and que, with no resource cleanup) and main then returns 0 (it ends without a return statement). It adds the mqprio qdisc and, with launch_time_delta_to_hw_rx_timestamp set, the etf qdisc, an ethtool rule (with a tc filter fallback) and VLAN offload through run_command, whose results are ignored except for the ethtool-rule test that selects the fallback. It then allocates rx_xsk (error(1, ENOMEM) on failure), opens an AF_XDP socket per queue, opens and loads the xdp_hw_metadata skeleton, starts the IPv6 UDP server on port 9092, fills the xsk map and attaches the XDP program; each of those failures calls error(1, ...) and terminates the process. It installs a SIGINT handler, runs verify_metadata, closes the server socket and calls cleanup(); a nonzero verify_metadata result calls error(1, ...) and terminates the process; otherwise it cleans the configurations again, frees buf, map and que, and returns 0.
note: reviewer (round15) right: run_command failures (tc/ethtool) are ignored (xdp_hw_metadata.c:806-825), they do not call error(1, ...); the old prose attributed termination to 'every other failure'. Slice cut the head.

name: clone_into_cgroup
prose: Precondition: cgroup_fd is an open file descriptor (typically a cgroup directory opened with O_PATH). Postcondition: attempts to create a child in the cgroup via clone3 with CLONE_INTO_CGROUP and SIGCHLD; on success it returns the child's pid in the parent and 0 in the child; if clone3 fails with ENOSYS or E2BIG, or if CLONE_ARGS_SIZE_VER2 is not defined at compile time, it sets errno to ENOSYS and returns -ENOSYS (-38); any other clone3 failure returns -1 with errno preserved. The function does not close cgroup_fd; the caller retains ownership of it.
note: re-checked against cgroup_util.c:394-420: prose matches (the -1/errno case for other clone3 failures is in the prose, so the round-0 reviewer's omission claim is wrong). Contract dropped because the function performs a system call (clone3) and the contract could not state the ENOSYS/E2BIG mapping (rejected mechanically in rounds 2/15).

name: TEST(close_range_cloexec)
prose: Test function generated by TEST(close_range_cloexec) (close_range_test.c:239-305); it takes the kselftest harness _metadata and returns void. Precondition: /dev/null can be opened 101 times. Postcondition: it opens /dev/null 101 times (ASSERT_GE; if an open fails with ENOENT it skips and returns). It then calls close_range(1000, 1000, CLOSE_RANGE_CLOEXEC) as a probe and skips and returns if that fails with ENOSYS or EINVAL. It lowers the soft RLIMIT_NOFILE to 25 (the limit is not restored), sets close-on-exec on the descriptor ranges open_fds[0]..open_fds[50] and open_fds[75]..open_fds[100] (each call asserted to return 0), and checks with fcntl(F_GETFD) that those 77 descriptors have FD_CLOEXEC and that the 24 descriptors open_fds[51]..open_fds[74] do not. It then calls close_range(3, UINT_MAX, CLOSE_RANGE_CLOEXEC) (result not checked) and checks that all 101 descriptors have FD_CLOEXEC. The descriptors are never closed by the test and remain open; each EXPECT_* records a failure without stopping the test, each ASSERT_* stops it.
note: slice cut the head; named by the TEST() invocation (generated function). Old prose (all 101 fds open with CLOEXEC, limit 25) is right for the end state but omitted the skip paths and the intermediate non-CLOEXEC check; not a reviewer claim.

name: TEST_F(coredump, socket_request_kernel)
prose: Test function generated by TEST_F(coredump, socket_request_kernel) (stackdump_test.c:727-850; the slice cut it short); it takes the harness _metadata and the fixture self and returns void. Precondition: the harness can set /proc/sys/kernel/core_pattern and create AF_UNIX sockets in /tmp. Postcondition: it sets the core pattern to '@@/tmp/coredump.socket', creates a socketpair and forks a coredump-server child. The child creates and listens on /tmp/coredump.socket, signals readiness over the socketpair, accepts the connection, obtains the peer pidfd and its info and requires PIDFD_INFO_COREDUMP with PIDFD_COREDUMPED set, creates /tmp/coredump.file, reads the coredump request and checks it for ACK size VER0 with the KERNEL, USERSPACE, REJECT and WAIT flags, sends an ack with KERNEL | WAIT, reads the REQACK marker, then copies everything read from the socket into the core file until end of file; it exits with EXIT_SUCCESS if every step passed, otherwise EXIT_FAILURE, closing its descriptors in both cases. The parent waits for the readiness byte, forks a child that crashes, opens its pidfd, waits for it and asserts that it was killed by a signal with a core dump, asserts that the pidfd info reports PIDFD_INFO_COREDUMP and PIDFD_COREDUMPED, calls wait_and_check_coredump_server, then asserts that /tmp/coredump.file exists with a size greater than 0 and runs 'file' on it. ASSERT_* failures stop the test, EXPECT_* failures are only recorded.
note: slice cut the head/tail; named by the TEST_F invocation (generated function). The dropped item's one-line prose is replaced after reading the whole test (stackdump_test.c:727-850).

name: TEST(mutex_state)
prose: Test function generated by TEST(mutex_state) (ntsync.c:225-377; the slice cut the head); it takes the harness _metadata and returns void. Precondition: /dev/ntsync can be opened (ASSERT_LE stops the test if it cannot). Postcondition: it records an EXPECT failure for each deviation from the expected NTSYNC mutex behavior and closes every mutex and the device fd it opened. It expects creating a mutex with owner 123 and count 0, or with owner 0 and count 2, to fail with -1/EINVAL; creating one with owner 123 and count 2 to succeed and report that state; unlock_mutex with owner 0 to fail with -1/EINVAL and with a non-owner (456) to fail with -1/EPERM leaving the state (2, 123); unlock by the owner to return 0 with the count before the decrement (2, then 1), the final unlock leaving state (count 0, owner 0); a further unlock on the now unowned mutex to fail with -1/EPERM; wait_any by owner 456 to return 0 with index 0 and take the mutex (count 1, then 2 on a recursive wait); wait_any by a different owner (123) while it is held to fail with -1/ETIMEDOUT; NTSYNC_IOC_MUTEX_KILL to fail with -1/EINVAL for owner 0 and -1/EPERM for a non-owner, and to return 0 for the current owner (456), after which NTSYNC_IOC_MUTEX_READ fails with -1/EOWNERDEAD with count 0 and owner 0, and wait_any fails with -1/EOWNERDEAD with index 0 but leaves the mutex acquired with count 1 and the waiter as owner (123), which can then itself be killed (return 0) with the same read/wait results. Finally it expects a new mutex created with owner 0 and count 0 to report that state and to be acquirable by wait_any (count 1, owner 123), and a mutex created with owner 123 and count ~0u to report that state and to make wait_any by owner 123 fail with -1/ETIMEDOUT.
note: slice cut the head; named by the TEST() invocation (generated function). Old prose said 'unlock_mutex with count 0' fails with EINVAL, but the test calls unlock_mutex(mutex, 0, ...), i.e. owner 0 (ntsync.c:255-257); it also omitted the creation errors and the unowned-unlock EPERM.

name: TEST(test_wait_any)
prose: Test function generated by TEST(test_wait_any) (ntsync.c:500-612; the slice starts in the middle of it); it takes the harness _metadata and returns void. Precondition: /dev/ntsync can be opened (ASSERT_LE stops the test otherwise). Postcondition: it records an EXPECT failure for each deviation from the expected NTSYNC wait-any behavior and closes the semaphore, the mutex it did not already close, and the device fd. It creates a semaphore (count 2, max 3) and a mutex (owner 0, count 0) and expects wait_any over both by owner 123 to return 0 with index 0 twice (the semaphore count goes 2 to 1 to 0, the mutex unchanged) and then index 1 (mutex acquired by 123 with count 1); after release_sem(1) (returning previous count 0) it expects index 0 again, then index 1 (mutex count 2); wait_any by owner 456 then fails with -1/ETIMEDOUT; after NTSYNC_IOC_MUTEX_KILL by owner 123 returns 0, wait_any by 456 fails with -1/EOWNERDEAD with index 1 and the next one succeeds with index 1. After closing the mutex it releases 2 on the semaphore, passes the semaphore twice in the object array and expects wait_any to return 0 with index 0 (semaphore count 1); wait_any with zero objects to fail with -1/ETIMEDOUT; wait_any with NTSYNC_MAX_WAIT_COUNT copies of the semaphore to return 0 with index 0; and wait_any with NTSYNC_MAX_WAIT_COUNT + 1 objects or with a count of -1 (as a __u32) to fail with -1/EINVAL.
note: slice cut the head; named by the TEST() invocation. The dropped item had no prose; written from ntsync.c:500-612.

name: FIXTURE_TEARDOWN(uvio_fixture)
prose: Fixture teardown generated by FIXTURE_TEARDOWN(uvio_fixture) (test_uvdevice.c:48-53), void; it takes the fixture data self. Precondition: self was filled in by the matching FIXTURE_SETUP (uv_fd from open of the uvdevice, fault_page from mmap). Postcondition: it calls close(self->uv_fd) whenever uv_fd is nonzero (including -1 after a failed open, in which case close fails harmlessly, so a -1 descriptor is not skipped; a descriptor value of 0 would not be closed) and then calls munmap on the page at self->fault_page of size getpagesize(); the return values of both calls are ignored.
note: reviewer (round15) right: the guard is 'if (self->uv_fd)' (test_uvdevice.c:50, 181), so -1 is nonzero and close(-1) is called; the old prose said a -1 descriptor is left untouched. Named by the macro invocation (method rule 5).

name: FIXTURE_TEARDOWN(attest_fixture)
prose: Fixture teardown generated by FIXTURE_TEARDOWN(attest_fixture) (test_uvdevice.c:179-184), void; it takes the fixture data self. Precondition: self was filled in by the matching FIXTURE_SETUP (uv_fd from open of the uvdevice, fault_page from mmap). Postcondition: it calls close(self->uv_fd) whenever uv_fd is nonzero (including -1 after a failed open, in which case close fails harmlessly, so a -1 descriptor is not skipped; a descriptor value of 0 would not be closed) and then calls munmap on the page at self->fault_page of size getpagesize(); the return values of both calls are ignored.
note: reviewer (round15) right: the guard is 'if (self->uv_fd)' (test_uvdevice.c:50, 181), so -1 is nonzero and close(-1) is called; the old prose said a -1 descriptor is left untouched. Named by the macro invocation (method rule 5).

name: main
prose: Precondition: main is called by the C runtime with argc/argv; the environment may define VERBOSE, CHECK_COMM and IN_TEST. Postcondition (main, execveat.c:446-520; slice cut the head): if argc >= 2 or CHECK_COMM is set, it runs no tests. With CHECK_COMM set it opens /proc/self/comm and calls exit(1) if open or read fails, strips the last character of what it read (buf[ret-1] is written even if read returned 0), calls exit(1) if the string differs from CHECK_COMM, and otherwise calls exit(0); it never returns on this path. With CHECK_COMM unset it returns 1 if IN_TEST is unset or not 'yes', and otherwise calls exit(atoi(argv[argc - 1])). Otherwise (argc < 2 and CHECK_COMM unset) it prints the ksft header, sets the plan to TESTS_EXPECTED, runs prerequisites, sets envp[1] to 'VERBOSE=1' when VERBOSE is set, calls run_tests, prints the number of failed tests if run_tests returned a positive value, and calls ksft_finished(), which exits the process (ksft_exit_pass or ksft_exit_fail, both noreturn) depending on whether the pass/xfail/xskip count equals the plan; the final 'return rc' is therefore not reached on that path. The only path on which main returns is the IN_TEST check failure (return 1).
note: slice cut the head; reviewer (round15) right: ksft_finished() expands to ksft_exit(...), which calls ksft_exit_pass/ksft_exit_fail (kselftest.h:372-402, __noreturn), so main does not return the failed-test count as the old prose said.

name: TEST_F_TIMEOUT(file_stressor, slab_typesafe_by_rcu, 900 * 2)
prose: Test function generated by TEST_F_TIMEOUT(file_stressor, slab_typesafe_by_rcu, 900 * 2) (file_stressor.c:109-192; harness timeout 1800 s); it takes _metadata and the fixture self and returns void. Precondition: the fixture setup has mounted a tmpfs at /slab_typesafe_by_rcu and allocated pids_openers, pids_getdents and fd_proc_pid for nr_procs processes, with max_fds = 500. Postcondition: it forks nr_procs opener children (ASSERT_GE on each fork); each child loops forever: for an index up to max_fds it opens (O_CREAT) a file named /slab_typesafe_by_rcu/file-<pid>-<index>, where the inner loop variable shadows the process index so the pid array is indexed by the file index, and then calls close_range(3, ~0U, 0). The parent then opens /proc/<opener pid>/fd/ as a directory descriptor for each opener (ASSERT_GE) and forks nr_procs getdents children; each child loops forever calling getdents64 on its descriptor while the call returns >= 0 (including 0 at the end of the directory), so the lseek back to 0 after that inner loop is reached only if getdents64 returns an error. The parent sleeps 900 seconds with clock_nanosleep (ASSERT_EQ 0), then sends SIGKILL to every opener and getdents child, and returns; reaping the children is left to the fixture teardown.
note: reviewer (round15) right: the 'do ... while (nr_read >= 0)' loop (file_stressor.c:176-178) exits only on a negative return, so lseek (180) is not reached after a normal 0 return; old prose's description of lseek in each pass was wrong. Also noted the shadowed loop variable at 122-126. Named by the TEST_F_TIMEOUT invocation (generated function).

name: FIXTURE_SETUP(iterate_mount_namespaces)
prose: Fixture setup generated by FIXTURE_SETUP(iterate_mount_namespaces) (iterate_mntns.c:49-63), void; it takes the fixture data self. Precondition: self points to the fixture data (fd_mnt_ns and mnt_ns_id arrays of MNT_NS_COUNT = 11 entries). Postcondition: it first sets every fd_mnt_ns entry to -EBADF. Then for each i from 0 to 10 it calls unshare(CLONE_NEWNS) (ASSERT_EQ 0), opens /proc/self/ns/mnt read-only with O_CLOEXEC into fd_mnt_ns[i] (ASSERT_GE 0), calls the NS_MNT_GET_INFO ioctl on it (ASSERT_EQ 0) and stores the reported mnt_ns_id in mnt_ns_id[i]. A failed ASSERT stops the test at once: entries before the failing one are complete, entries after it are still -EBADF, and the failing entry holds whatever the failing step left (the negative result of a failed open, or an open descriptor without its mnt_ns_id set when only the ioctl failed). On success all 11 descriptors are open and mnt_ns_id holds the 11 ids.
note: reviewer (round15) right: the entry being processed when open or the ioctl fails is not -EBADF (iterate_mntns.c:58-61); the old prose said the remaining entries (after the failure) are -EBADF, which is true only for later entries. Named by the macro invocation (method rule 5).

name: TEST_F(set_layers_via_fds, set_override_creds)
prose: Test function generated by TEST_F(set_layers_via_fds, set_override_creds) (set_layers_via_fds.c:231-329; the slice starts mid-test); it takes _metadata and self and returns void. Precondition: the test can unshare a mount namespace (CAP_SYS_ADMIN in its user namespace), /tmp and /set_layers_via_fds exist (the fixture creates the latter), and the kernel supports overlayfs layer fds. Postcondition: it unshares CLONE_NEWNS and makes / a recursive slave mount, creates a tmpfs through fsopen/fsconfig/fsmount, creates directories w, u, l1 and l2 in it, opens them as layer_fds[0..3], moves the tmpfs mount to /tmp and closes the tmpfs fd. It opens an overlay filesystem context and asserts that setting 'lowerdir' from a layer fd fails, then sets workdir (layer 0), upperdir (layer 1), lowerdir+ (layers 2 and 3) from fds and 'metacopy=on'. It then forks three children in turn, each calling fsconfig on the shared context with the flag override_creds, nooverride_creds and override_creds respectively; the child exits with EXIT_FAILURE (and logs) if its fsconfig fails, but the parent only waits for each child (waitid) and closes its pidfd without checking the child's exit status. It creates the overlay superblock (FSCONFIG_CMD_CREATE), fsmounts it, moves the mount to /set_layers_via_fds and closes the context and overlay fds. Every ASSERT_* failure stops the test. The four layer descriptors layer_fds[] are never closed by the test.
note: slice cut the head; named by the TEST_F invocation (generated function). Old prose claimed every fd opened by the test is closed and that the children's acceptance is verified; the layer fds are not closed and the child exit status is not checked (set_layers_via_fds.c:254-264, 281-318).

name: TEST(priv_hash)
prose: Test function generated by TEST(priv_hash) (futex_priv_hash.c:134-268; the slice stops at line 251); it takes the harness _metadata and returns void. Precondition: a fresh process in which the private futex hash has not been set up yet, on a kernel supporting PR_FUTEX_HASH. Postcondition: it initializes a priority-inheritance mutex (exiting the process with a failure message if that fails) and requires PR_FUTEX_HASH_GET_SLOTS to return 0 (otherwise it exits with a failure message); after creating and joining one thread it requires the slot count to be positive (else exits). It then locks global_lock, resets counter, creates MAX_THREADS (64) threads that wait on a barrier, then take the lock and increment counter, and releases them through the barrier; when more than 16 CPUs are online it polls the slot count (up to 20 tries, doing a 100 ms timed lock between tries) for an automatic increase and exits with a failure message if none appears, otherwise (16 CPUs or fewer) it records a skip; it unlocks global_lock. It sets the slot count to 2, 4, 8, 32 and 16, each time reading it back (a failed set or a different value records a failure and calls ksft_finished, which exits), expects setting 15 to fail, sets 2 again, joins the threads and records whether counter equals MAX_THREADS. It resets counter and the barrier, creates and joins MAX_THREADS threads again and records whether the slot count is still 2 (no automatic resize after a manual setting), expects setting 1 << 29 to fail and sets 4 again. It then requests the global hash by setting 0 slots and records the result; if that set fails it returns at once (the global hash was not requested, and the remaining checks are skipped). Otherwise it expects setting 4, 8, 8, 0 and 6 slots to fail, runs MAX_THREADS threads once more and records whether the slot count is 0 (the global hash stays in use).
note: reviewer (round15) right: when set(0) fails the test returns before the global hash has been requested (futex_priv_hash.c:248-251); old prose said it was already requested and omitted the later global-hash phase (253-267); round-0 reviewer's omission points are covered. Named by the TEST() invocation (generated function).

name: TEST_F(iommufd_ioas, iova_ranges)
prose: Test function generated by TEST_F(iommufd_ioas, iova_ranges) (iommufd.c:1064-1138, followed by further checks); it takes _metadata and the fixture self and returns void. Precondition: self->fd and self->ioas_id are valid; self->stdev_id says whether a mock device is attached. Postcondition: it calls IOMMU_IOAS_IOVA_RANGES with a buffer for BUFFER_SIZE / sizeof(range) entries (ASSERT_EQ 0) and expects exactly 1 range: [0, SIZE_MAX] with out_iova_alignment 1 when there is no mock device, or [MOCK_APERTURE_START, MOCK_APERTURE_LAST] with alignment MOCK_PAGE_SIZE when there is. With num_iovas = 0 and a zeroed buffer it expects errno EMSGSIZE, num_iovas set to 1 and the buffer still zero. It then adds a reserved range [PAGE_SIZE, 2 * PAGE_SIZE) via IOMMU_TEST_OP_ADD_RESERVED and expects 2 ranges ([0, PAGE_SIZE - 1] and [2 * PAGE_SIZE, SIZE_MAX]) without a mock device or still the single aperture range with one. With a zeroed buffer and num_iovas = 1 it expects, without a mock device, errno EMSGSIZE with num_iovas set to 2 and the first range ([0, PAGE_SIZE - 1]) copied into ranges[0], and with a mock device a success returning the one aperture range. Each EXPECT_* records a failure and continues; each ASSERT_* stops the test.
note: slice cut at the end (the test continues); named by the TEST_F invocation. Reviewer (round15) right: when the supplied buffer is too small the kernel still copies as many ranges as fit (ranges[0] is expected to be filled when num_iovas = 1), so 'array untouched on EMSGSIZE' is false (iommufd.c:1122-1128); it is untouched only in the num_iovas = 0 case.

name: TEST_F(iommufd_ioas, access_rw)
prose: Precondition: the fixture's ioas_id and fd are valid and buffer holds BUFFER_SIZE bytes. Postcondition: an access is created, buffer is mapped, check_access_rw succeeds both with flags 0 and with MOCK_ACCESS_RW_SLOW_PATH, then the mapping is unmapped and the access destroyed; the function returns void and aborts the test on any assertion failure.
note: unreviewed (round15 fixed-unreviewed); prose kept after re-reading iommufd.c:1334-1346; named by the TEST_F invocation (generated function)

name: TEST_F(iommufd_ioas, fork_gone)
prose: Precondition: the fixture's ioas_id and fd are valid. Postcondition: after a forked child maps MOCK_APERTURE_START and exits and is reaped, if self->stdev_id is set a mock domain is created and check_access_rw succeeds at MOCK_APERTURE_START, otherwise mock domain creation is expected to fail with EFAULT; the access is then destroyed and the function returns void, aborting the test on any assertion failure.
note: unreviewed (round15 fixed-unreviewed); prose re-checked against iommufd.c:1363-1398 and kept; named by the TEST_F invocation (generated function)

name: TEST_F(iommufd_ioas, fork_present)
prose: Precondition: the fixture's ioas_id and fd are valid. Postcondition: after the child maps MOCK_APERTURE_START, signals through the eventfd and blocks on the pipe, the parent reads 8 bytes from the eventfd, creates a mock domain, check_access_rw succeeds at MOCK_APERTURE_START, the pipe is closed, the child is reaped and the access destroyed; the function returns void and aborts the test on any assertion failure.
note: unreviewed (round15 fixed-unreviewed); prose re-checked against iommufd.c:1400-1441 and kept; named by the TEST_F invocation (generated function)

name: TEST_F(iommufd_ioas, ioas_option_huge_pages)
prose: Precondition: the fixture's ioas_id and fd are valid. Postcondition: IOMMU_OPTION GET of IOMMU_OPTION_HUGE_PAGES returns 1, SET 0 succeeds and a following GET returns 0, SET 2 fails with EINVAL, and SET 1 succeeds; the function returns void and aborts the test on any assertion failure.
note: unreviewed (round15 fixed-unreviewed); prose re-checked against iommufd.c:1443-1472 and kept; named by the TEST_F invocation (generated function)

name: TEST_F(iommufd_ioas, ioas_iova_alloc)
prose: Precondition: the fixture's ioas_id and fd are valid and variant->mock_domains is readable. Postcondition: for every length from 1 to PAGE_SIZE*2-1, if mock_domains is set and length is not a multiple of MOCK_PAGE_SIZE the map ioctl fails with EINVAL, otherwise the buffer maps and unmaps successfully; the function returns void and aborts the test on any assertion failure.
note: unreviewed (round15 fixed-unreviewed); prose re-checked against iommufd.c:1474-1487 and kept; named by the TEST_F invocation (generated function)

name: TEST_F(iommufd_ioas, ioas_align_change)
prose: Precondition: the fixture's ioas_id and fd are valid and variant->mock_domains is false (the test returns immediately otherwise). Postcondition: a PAGE_SIZE fixed map at MOCK_APERTURE_START succeeds, setting alignment 0 succeeds, a misaligned fixed map fails with EINVAL, setting alignment 0 again succeeds, setting alignment 1 succeeds, a fixed map at MOCK_APERTURE_START+PAGE_SIZE succeeds, setting alignment 0 then fails with EADDRINUSE, and both mappings are unmapped; the function returns void and aborts the test on any assertion failure.
note: unreviewed (round15 fixed-unreviewed); prose re-checked against iommufd.c:1489-1531 and kept; named by the TEST_F invocation (generated function)

name: TEST_F(iommufd_ioas, copy_sweep)
prose: Test function generated by TEST_F(iommufd_ioas, copy_sweep) (iommufd.c:1533-1573); it takes _metadata, the fixture self and the variant, and returns void. Precondition: self->fd and self->ioas_id are valid. Postcondition: it allocates a second IOAS (dst_ioas_id) and maps the test buffer at MOCK_APERTURE_START in the source IOAS up to last_iova (MOCK_APERTURE_START + BUFFER_SIZE - 1 with mock domains, one byte less otherwise). It then sweeps iova from MOCK_APERTURE_START - PAGE_SIZE up to last_iova in steps of 511 and copies MOCK_PAGE_SIZE bytes from each source iova into the destination IOAS at MOCK_APERTURE_START with IOMMU_IOAS_COPY: when the source range starts before MOCK_APERTURE_START or ends after last_iova it expects errno ENOENT (EXPECT_ERRNO, recorded and continuing); otherwise it asserts that the copy succeeds and unmaps the copied range from the destination IOAS. Finally it destroys the destination IOAS.
note: slice cut; the dropped item had a one-line truncated prose; written from iommufd.c:1533-1573. Named by the TEST_F invocation.

name: TEST_F(iommufd_mock_domain, all_aligns)
prose: Test function generated by TEST_F(iommufd_mock_domain, all_aligns) (iommufd.c:1784-1836); it takes _metadata, the fixture self and the variant, and returns void. Precondition: self->fd and self->ioas_id are valid; self->mmap_buf_size and self->mmap_flags are set. Postcondition: it creates its own buffer of mmap_buf_size bytes, with memfd_mmap (MAP_SHARED, giving mfd) in the file variant or mmap otherwise, asserts it is mapped (and mfd > 0 for the file variant), and checks that no page references exist. It then sweeps start from 0 in steps of MOCK_PAGE_SIZE (mmap_buf_size / 16 in the hugepages variant) and, for each, end values from start + MOCK_PAGE_SIZE in steps of MOCK_PAGE_SIZE while end < mmap_buf_size: it maps [start, end) into the IOAS (from the file offset in the file variant, else from buf + start), checks the mock iova contents, checks that the covered pages (rounded to PAGE_SIZE) hold one reference, and unmaps the range. In the hugepages variant end starts at mmap_buf_size, so the inner loop body does not run. Afterwards it checks that all page references are 0, munmaps the buffer (ASSERT_EQ 0) and closes mfd in the file variant.
note: unreviewed (round15 fixed-unreviewed); corrected: the buffer is created inside the test (the old precondition said the caller supplies it) and in the hugepages variant the inner loop never executes (iommufd.c:1809-1813). Named by the TEST_F invocation.

name: TEST_F(iommufd_mock_domain, all_aligns_copy)
prose: Test function generated by TEST_F(iommufd_mock_domain, all_aligns_copy) (iommufd.c:1838-1901); it takes _metadata, the fixture self and the variant, and returns void. Precondition: self->fd, self->ioas_id and self->hwpt_ids are set up by the fixture. Postcondition: like all_aligns it creates its own buffer of mmap_buf_size bytes (memfd_mmap in the file variant, mmap otherwise), checks that no page references exist, and sweeps start and end in MOCK_PAGE_SIZE steps (the hugepages variant has start steps of mmap_buf_size / 16 and an end that begins at mmap_buf_size, so its inner loop body does not run). For each range it maps [start, end) into the IOAS, then adds a mock domain on self->ioas_id while the area exists (saving and later restoring self->hwpt_ids[1]), checks the mock iova contents and that the covered pages hold one reference, destroys the mock device, restores hwpt_ids[1] and unmaps the range. Afterwards it checks that page references are 0, munmaps the buffer and closes mfd in the file variant.
note: unreviewed (round15 fixed-unreviewed); corrected: the buffer is created inside the test and the hugepages variant's inner loop does not run (iommufd.c:1862-1867). Named by the TEST_F invocation.

name: TEST_F(iommufd_mock_domain, user_copy)
prose: Test function generated by TEST_F(iommufd_mock_domain, user_copy) (iommufd.c:1903-1976); it takes _metadata, the fixture self and the variant, and returns void. Precondition: the source buffer (mfd_buffer in the file variant, otherwise buffer) of BUFFER_SIZE bytes is accessible, self->ioas_id is a valid IOAS and the BUFFER_SIZE range at MOCK_APERTURE_START is free in it. Postcondition: it allocates a temporary IOAS (ioas_id) with no domains, maps the buffer into it (from the memfd in the file variant), creates an access object on it that needs pinned pages and pins the pages with IOMMU_TEST_OP_ACCESS_PAGES; it copies the mapping from that IOAS into self->ioas_id at MOCK_APERTURE_START (IOMMU_IOAS_COPY) and checks the mock iova contents. It then allocates a new IOAS, maps the buffer into it, moves the access to it (test_cmd_access_replace_ioas), unmaps the copied range at MOCK_APERTURE_START from self->ioas_id and destroys the temporary IOAS ioas_id. It then pins the pages again, copies from the new IOAS into self->ioas_id at MOCK_APERTURE_START and checks the contents, and finally destroys the access pages, the access object and the new IOAS. ASSERT_* failures stop the test.
note: unreviewed (round15 fixed-unreviewed); corrected: the unmapped copied mapping is the one in the destination self->ioas_id (iommufd.c:1919-1924, 1959), and the old IOAS being destroyed is the temporary source IOAS. Named by the TEST_F invocation.

name: TEST_F(iommufd_mock_domain, replace)
prose: Test function generated by TEST_F(iommufd_mock_domain, replace) (iommufd.c:1978-2006); it takes _metadata, the fixture self and the variant, and returns void. Precondition: self->stdev_ids[0], self->hwpt_ids and self->ioas_id are valid. Postcondition: it allocates a new IOAS and replaces the IOAS attached to stdev_ids[0] with it; with exactly one mock domain it expects replacing back to self->hwpt_ids[0] to fail with ENOENT (the previous hwpt was deallocated); it replaces with the new IOAS again; with two or more mock domains it replaces with self->hwpt_ids[1] twice and then self->hwpt_ids[0]; it finally attaches the device to self->ioas_id and destroys the temporary IOAS. Helper failures stop the test.
note: unreviewed (round15 fixed-unreviewed); added the second replace with the temporary IOAS (iommufd.c:1994) which the old prose omitted. Named by the TEST_F invocation.

name: TEST_F(iommufd_mock_domain, alloc_hwpt)
prose: Test function generated by TEST_F(iommufd_mock_domain, alloc_hwpt) (iommufd.c:2008-2036); it takes _metadata, the fixture self and the variant, and returns void. Precondition: for each i below variant->mock_domains the fixture's idev_ids[i] and stdev_ids[i] exist and self->ioas_id is valid. Postcondition: for each mock device it expects hwpt allocation with the flags ~IOMMU_HWPT_ALLOC_NEST_PARENT to fail with EOPNOTSUPP, and allocation with flags 0 and with IOMMU_HWPT_ALLOC_NEST_PARENT to succeed (hwpt_id[0], hwpt_id[1]). It then attaches the device to hwpt_id[0] and expects destroying hwpt_id[0] to fail with EBUSY (EXPECT_ERRNO), does the same with hwpt_id[1], re-attaches the device to self->ioas_id, destroys hwpt_id[1], creates a mock domain on hwpt_id[0] and destroys that mock device, and destroys hwpt_id[0].
note: unreviewed (round15 fixed-unreviewed); prose re-read against iommufd.c:2008-2036 and kept. Named by the TEST_F invocation.

name: FIXTURE_SETUP(iommufd_dirty_tracking)
prose: Fixture setup generated by FIXTURE_SETUP(iommufd_dirty_tracking) (iommufd.c:2057-2125), void; it takes the fixture data self and the variant. Precondition: variant->buffer_size and variant->hugepages are set. Postcondition: if variant->buffer_size is smaller than MOCK_PAGE_SIZE it skips the test and returns before touching self. Otherwise it opens /dev/iommu into self->fd (ASSERT_NE -1) and allocates self->buffer with posix_memalign aligned to HUGEPAGE_SIZE: of variant->buffer_size bytes normally, or of max(buffer_size, HUGEPAGE_SIZE) bytes in the hugepages variant, which then maps it in place with MAP_HUGETLB | MAP_POPULATE; if the allocation fails it skips and returns (self->fd stays open). It maps self->buffer in place with mmap (assert that the address is unchanged), sets self->page_size to MOCK_PAGE_SIZE and self->bitmap_size to buffer_size / MOCK_PAGE_SIZE, and allocates self->bitmap, PAGE_SIZE-aligned, of DIV_ROUND_UP(bitmap_size, BITS_PER_BYTE) + PAGE_SIZE bytes. It then allocates an IOAS in self->ioas_id and creates the mock domain, device and hwpt (self->stdev_id, hwpt_id, idev_id), with MOCK_FLAGS_DEVICE_HUGE_IOVA when variant->hugepages is set.
note: reviewer (round15) right: on buffer allocation failure the fd is already open (iommufd.c:2071-2098), and only the hugepage variant rounds the allocation up to HUGEPAGE_SIZE (2090-2091); the old prose said max(buffer_size, HUGEPAGE_SIZE) always. Named by the macro invocation (method rule 5).

name: iommufd_ioas_hwpt_invalidate_test
note: not a function: no such name exists; the slice shows the tail of TEST_F(iommufd_ioas, alloc_hwpt_nested) (iommufd.c:430-720, whose hwpt-invalidate checks are at 528-668) followed by the small tests hwpt_attach, ioas_area_destroy and ioas_area_auto_destroy; none of these is listed as an item

name: TEST_F(iommufd_ioas, get_hw_info)
prose: Test function generated by TEST_F(iommufd_ioas, get_hw_info) (iommufd.c:754-810; the slice starts mid-test, and the packet name iommufd_ioas_hw_page_table_based_test does not exist); it takes _metadata, the fixture self and the variant, and returns void. Precondition: self->fd is valid; self->device_id is nonzero when the fixture has a device. Postcondition: when self->device_id is nonzero it queries hardware info for the device with a zero-size buffer and with an exact-size buffer (IOMMU_HW_INFO_TYPE_DEFAULT), expects a query with the wrong type IOMMU_HW_INFO_TYPE_SELFTEST + 1 to fail with EOPNOTSUPP and a query with IOMMU_HW_INFO_TYPE_SELFTEST to succeed, queries with a larger buffer (the helper checks that the kernel zeroes the trailing bytes) and with a smaller buffer (the fields within the given size are still updated), then asserts that the PASID query for self->device_id reports a maximum PASID of 0 and, when variant->pasid_capable is set, that the one for self->device_pasid_id reports MOCK_PASID_WIDTH. When self->device_id is zero it expects the exact-size and larger-buffer queries to fail with ENOENT. Helper checks abort the test on failure.
note: slice cut the head; the old (dropped) prose described this test under the name iommufd_ioas_hw_page_table_based_test and is rewritten from iommufd.c:754-810. Named by the TEST_F invocation.

name: TEST_F(iommufd_ioas, area_auto_iova)
prose: Test function generated by TEST_F(iommufd_ioas, area_auto_iova) (iommufd.c:884-969); it takes _metadata and the fixture self and returns void. Precondition: self->fd and self->ioas_id are valid; buffer is the test's mapped buffer; self->stdev_id is nonzero when a mock device is attached. Postcondition: it maps and unmaps ten one-page areas at automatically chosen iovas; then for lengths PAGE_SIZE * (i + 1), i from 0 to 9, it maps each (the buffer when self->stdev_id is set, otherwise the fixed address 1UL << 31), expects each returned iova to be aligned to 1UL << (ffs(length) - 1) (EXPECT_EQ) and unmaps them. It adds a reserved range [4 * PAGE_SIZE, 104 * PAGE_SIZE) (ASSERT_EQ 0), maps the buffer ten more times with those lengths, expecting the same alignment and that no iova lies strictly inside the reserved range, and unmaps them. It expects IOMMU_IOAS_ALLOW_IOVAS for [PAGE_SIZE, 600 * PAGE_SIZE] to fail with EADDRINUSE (it overlaps the reserved range), then allows [MOCK_APERTURE_START + PAGE_SIZE, MOCK_APERTURE_START + 600 * PAGE_SIZE - 1] with a mock device or [200 * PAGE_SIZE, 600 * PAGE_SIZE - 1] without (ASSERT_EQ 0), maps the buffer ten more times with those lengths and expects each to be aligned and to lie within the allowed range, and unmaps them. EXPECT_* failures are recorded and continue; ASSERT_* failures stop the test.
note: reviewer (round15) right: the buffer is mapped unconditionally in the first, third and fourth loops (iommufd.c:905, 931, 960); only the second loop chooses between buffer and the fixed address 1UL << 31 by stdev_id (913-918). Named by the TEST_F invocation.

name: fail_nth_next
prose:
Precondition: nth_state->proc_fd is an open fail-nth file descriptor, _metadata is the harness metadata, test_result is only used in a commented-out print. Postcondition (fail_nth_next, iommufd_fail_nth.c:102-155): it asserts that nth_state->iteration is below 1000 (ASSERT_GT, aborting the test otherwise). When iteration is 0 it just increments iteration and returns true. Otherwise it first reads the fail-nth file with pread (if that fails with EFAULT it substitutes the text '1
' with length 2), then writes '0' to the file to disable injection (if that write fails with EFAULT it retries once and sets the text to '1
'), asserts that exactly 1 byte was written and that the read length is greater than 1 (both abort the test on failure). If the text read was exactly '0
' it increments iteration and returns true; for any other text (including the substituted '1
') it returns false without incrementing iteration.
note:
reviewer (round15) right: the read-back happens before the disable write (iommufd_fail_nth.c:126-134), and a read length <= 1 or a failed write aborts through ASSERT_* instead of returning false; round-0 reviewer's EFAULT-in-pwrite point is covered by the substituted '1
' case.

name: __TEST_F_IMPL(fixture_name, test_name, signal, tmout)
prose: Generated function wrapper_<fixture_name>_<test_name>(_metadata, variant) (defined inside __TEST_F_IMPL, kselftest_harness.h:411-461); static void. Precondition: _metadata is the test's metadata and variant the fixture variant descriptor. Postcondition: it mmaps a shared _metadata->no_teardown flag (result not checked); if the fixture data type has nonzero size it allocates self as a shared anonymous mapping when the fixture uses FIXTURE_TEARDOWN_PARENT, otherwise as a zeroed local variable. It stores variant->data and self in _metadata and forks. In the child it runs the fixture setup and, if setup left _metadata->exit_code nonzero, calls _exit(0) at once; otherwise it runs the test body, calls the teardown wrapper with in_parent = false and calls _exit(0). In the parent, if fork failed or waitpid did not return the child it prints an error and sets _metadata->exit_code = KSFT_FAIL; it then calls the teardown wrapper with in_parent = true, unmaps no_teardown (setting it to NULL) and unmaps self if it was a shared mapping; only after that does it examine the child's status: a normal exit with a nonzero status is stored in _metadata->exit_code, and a death by signal prints a message and re-raises that signal on the calling process with kill(getpid(), ...). It returns void.
note: reviewer (round15) right: the parent-side teardown and the unmaps happen before the child status handling and signal re-raise (kselftest_harness.h:449-460), not after as the old prose said. Named by the macro head (method rule 5) because the function name is generated.

name: __TEST_F_IMPL(fixture_name, test_name, signal, tmout)
prose: Generated function wrapper_<fixture_name>_<test_name>_teardown(in_parent, _metadata, self, variant) (defined inside __TEST_F_IMPL, kselftest_harness.h:462-469); static void. Precondition: _metadata->no_teardown points to the shared bool allocated by the test wrapper. Postcondition: it calls the fixture's teardown function with (_metadata, self, variant) only if the fixture's teardown_parent flag equals in_parent and the atomic test-and-set of *_metadata->no_teardown finds it previously clear (so the teardown runs at most once across the child and the parent); otherwise it does nothing. It returns void.
note: reviewer (round15) concern (parent-side ordering) concerns the test wrapper, not this function, so the old prose is kept in substance; re-read kselftest_harness.h:462-469. Named by the macro head (method rule 5).

name: __TEST_F_IMPL(fixture_name, test_name, signal, tmout)
prose: Generated function _register_<fixture_name>_<test_name>(void) (defined inside __TEST_F_IMPL, kselftest_harness.h:471-484); static void, declared as a constructor with priority KSELFTEST_PRIO_TEST so it runs before main. Precondition: the fixture object _<fixture_name>_fixture_object is defined. Postcondition: it mmaps a shared struct __test_metadata (result not checked), sets its name to the test name, fn to wrapper_<fixture_name>_<test_name>, fixture to the fixture object, teardown_fn to wrapper_<fixture_name>_<test_name>_teardown, termsig to the signal argument and timeout to the tmout argument, stores the pointer in the file-static _<fixture_name>_<test_name>_object, and registers it with __register_test. It returns void.
note: reviewer (round15) concern (parent-side ordering) does not apply to this function; old prose kept in substance after re-reading kselftest_harness.h:471-484. Named by the macro head (method rule 5).
